audit_findings.title: Unbridged derivative liabilities may rank ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $94 million net derivative liability at 2026-06-30, computed from $142 million liabilities less $48 million assets; even deducting the full $142 million gross liabilities equals $0.73 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any derivative settlement obligation not offset by hedged debt, operating cash flows, assets, or forecast OE requires an equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the net fair value of all financial instruments with exposure to currency risk was a $163 million liability.
audit_findings.explanation: The liabilities are demonstrated, but an unoffset claim is not: the filing identifies the instruments as hedges and reports no hedge ineffectiveness. Even the conservative deduction of all $142 million of derivative liabilities while ignoring $48 million of derivative assets would reduce base value from $20.04 to about $19.31 per share and bull value from $23.50 to about $22.77, leaving both below the $27.97 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each latest derivative asset and liability to its hedged debt, forecast transaction, or net investment and rerun only for any residual settlement claim not already reflected in OE or an offsetting balance-sheet item.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may understate required forward reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: 2026 first-half capital expenditures were $46 million versus $41 million in the 2025 first half, a filed $5 million increase; the full-year increase and required-maintenance portion are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Required capital spending reduces forward OE; spending necessary to obtain modeled growth must be deducted before applying the growth scenarios.
audit_findings.evidence: For 2026, we expect capital expenditures to increase relative to 2025, primarily due to new or additional investments in our zero emissions technology portfolio.
audit_findings.explanation: This is more than a purely hypothetical warning because capital spending has already increased, but the record does not separate maintenance, defensive transition spending, and discretionary growth investment. The filed $5 million interim increase alone does not establish a material valuation error, while the unquantified future program prevents a reliable materiality ceiling.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2026 capital-expenditure budget and subsequent actuals by project, classify maintenance and scenario-enabling investment, and rerun OE and all scenarios with the required annual deductions.

audit_findings.title: Non-service pension income may be embedded in recurring OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $15 million of filed 2025 non-service pension income; maximum no-tax perpetuation effect is approximately $199 million of base value or $1.02 per share, computed using the base operating-PV-to-anchor multiple
audit_findings.mechanism: If included in the $282.9 million anchor, non-service pension income raises OE despite being driven by plan returns, actuarial items, and other non-operating components rather than recurring operating cash generation.
audit_findings.evidence: The adjustment for other non-operating income reflects the non-service component of net periodic pension costs and other income that are not considered directly related to the Company's operations.
audit_findings.explanation: Inclusion in the anchor is unresolved, so this is not a demonstrated error. Even assuming the entire $15 million was included, receives no tax reduction, and recurs throughout the DCF, base value would be about $21.06 per share and bull value about $24.70 per share, still below the $27.97 market price and within the valuation's 30% margin-of-safety structure.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $15 million from net income through every OE adjustment; if included, remove it and substitute expected cash pension contributions or a supportable sustainable pension cost, then rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Existing uncertain-tax claims may be absent from both OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $91 million at 2025 year-end, comprising $55 million of unrecognized tax benefits and $36 million of accrued interest and penalties; latest filed income-tax liabilities were $93 million, equal to $0.48 per diluted valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: Settlement of an already accrued tax exposure can consume cash without a corresponding future OE expense, requiring a bridge deduction unless forecast cash taxes already capture it.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023 there were $ 55 million, $ 48 million, and $ 66 million, respectively, of unrecognized tax benefits that, if recognized, would be recorded as a component of tax expense.
audit_findings.explanation: The claims are demonstrated and appear within balance-sheet tax liabilities, while their omission from forecast cash taxes remains unresolved. Deducting the entire latest $93 million liability would reduce base value from $20.04 to about $19.56 per share and bull value from $23.50 to about $23.02, which does not change the conclusion relative to the $27.97 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $93 million latest tax-liability balance to uncertain tax benefits, interest, penalties, and ordinary current taxes; deduct probable settlement amounts not represented in forecast OE and document any expected releases.

audit_findings.title: The full cash add-back may not be distributable to the parent
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum identified exposure is the full $158 million cash add-back, equal to $0.81 per diluted valuation share and 4.0% of base equity value; the actually restricted amount is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash that cannot be transferred after local liquidity needs, taxes, exchange controls, or covenants should be excluded from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Certain countries in which we operate have adopted or could institute currency exchange controls that limit or prohibit our local subsidiaries' ability to convert local currency into U.S. dollars or to make payments outside the country.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the possibility of restrictions but identifies no trapped amount. Even treating all $158 million as unavailable would reduce base value to about $19.23 per share, bull value to about $22.69, and buy-below value by about $0.57; the valuation would remain below the $27.97 market price in every scenario.
audit_findings.action: Map the $158 million by jurisdiction and legal entity, quantify transfer taxes, controls, covenants, and minimum operating cash, and replace the add-back with verified distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Transaction-related costs may have been capitalized into the perpetual anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $12 million of filed 2025 costs: $6 million of M&A professional fees and $6 million of debt-refinancing costs; maximum no-tax normalization effect is approximately $160 million of base value or $0.82 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If included in the $282.9 million latest-actual anchor and then grown perpetually, genuinely nonrecurring transaction costs suppress OE and intrinsic value.
audit_findings.evidence: A $7 million reduction in personnel costs related to cost measures implemented in current and prior years and $5 million of lower outsourced activities were offset by $7 million of unfavorable foreign currency impacts and $6 million in professional fees related to merger and acquisition activity.
audit_findings.explanation: The expenses are demonstrated, but their inclusion in anchor OE and complete nonrecurrence are not. Even adding back the full $12 million without a tax reduction would raise base value only to about $20.86 per share and bull value to about $24.46, still below the $27.97 market price; any tax adjustment or recurring advisory burden would reduce the effect further.
audit_findings.action: Trace both $6 million cost categories through the OE calculation, determine which amounts are genuinely nonrecurring, and rerun the valuation only for the supported after-tax normalization.
